_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); railroad signals

pit_profile.why: Union Pacific: the largest railroad in North America, covering 23 states across the western two-thirds of the US, with BNSF its main rail competitor on parallel routes; carload volume follows the industrial economy, the franchise does not

classification.quality_note: Union Pacific: the largest railroad in North America, covering 23 states across the western two-thirds of the US, with BNSF its main rail competitor on parallel routes; carload volume follows the industrial economy, the franchise does not. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price rich; +119% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap -1.19; conservative 2yr -30%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -17.4%/yr (worst year FY08-FY17, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +10.8%/yr (Q2 2018 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +11.0%/yr (FY08-FY17 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +34.0%/yr (best 2-yr run FY08-FY17); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: UNP (retrospective, 2018-09-21) ✕ AVOID — Ratio B infx (68.5% downside to Bear $52 / +-20.6% upside to Bull $131) | Adj composite 2.58 vs market 3.77: gap -1.19 [OVERVALUED] | +119% above the EPP floor $75 (13x FY18E $5.79) | Conservative 2-yr case: -29.9% total (-14.9%/yr) | At 28.5x FY18E the 15% hurdle price $218 sits above the BULL case; carloads +4% in Q2 2018, forward revenue +8% (no FY18 revenue guide, Q2 2018 freight revenue); no disruption theme has dated evidence.

sources.title: Union Pacific Corporation 8-K (Item 7.01): Investor Day financial guidance
sources.supports: positive annual volume growth over the next three years (words only); a 60% operating ratio on a full year basis by 2020; capital expenditures at or below 15% of revenue; about $20 billion of share repurchases over three years inclusive of 2018; a 40-45% dividend payout ratio target; adjusted debt to EBITDA of up to 2.7
